findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the vendor-roster.xlsx seed object) are stored unencrypted by default, violating encryption-at-rest requirements for stored data.
This bucket stores ledger/financial export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving sensitive financial records unencrypted at rest.
Despite having versioning and logging configured, this bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving model artifacts unencrypted at rest.
This bucket stores operational runbooks but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving potentially sensitive operational documentation unencrypted at rest.
The uploaded object does not specify server_side_encryption and is placed in a bucket (reports_archive) that also lacks default encryption, so this file is stored in cleartext.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket, so there is no explicit enforcement preventing future public ACLs or bucket policies from exposing its contents.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this sensitive ledger data bucket, leaving it without an explicit safeguard against accidental public exposure via ACL or policy changes.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket, so there is no explicit enforcement preventing accidental public exposure of model artifacts.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket, so there is no explicit enforcement preventing accidental public exposure of operational runbooks.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is associated with this bucket; although the ACL is log-delivery-write, the absence of an explicit block leaves it reliant on account-level defaults to prevent public exposure.
